headline: Across five national polls this year, between 55% and 77% of Americans say AI is moving too fast or should slow down, a Tech Policy Press roundup finds.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a useful roundup of consistent public opinion with a policy angle, but the polls word their questions differently and the per-poll figures were not readable in the text.
importance_line: American voters across party lines are telling pollsters they want a slower pace while the Trump administration rejects a slowdown, which matters first to voters and lawmakers before the midterms, then to AI companies; the polls word their questions differently, so the range is not a trend.
summary: Tech Policy Press, a technology-policy news outlet, reports that in five national polls in 2026 the share of American adults saying AI is moving too fast, or should slow down, ranged from 55% to 77%; Democrats were more concerned than Republicans, but in three of the four polls that broke results out by party a majority of Republicans also said AI was moving too fast. It notes that each pollster worded its question differently, so the results are not a trend, and that President Donald Trump has rejected calls for a slowdown, saying "whoever wins AI, wins", a stance the Washington Post reports Democrats are using as a line of attack in the midterm elections.
notes: Full text read; the per-poll results sat in charts that were not captured as text, so the range ends cannot be tied to named polls. The article was built with an AI tool and says its details were checked against sources. Polls date from January to 5 Oct 2026; the roundup was published 13 Oct.
